title: Canary scripting and automated rollback scorer for private control plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) control plane upgrades are high-risk: subtle regressions in control-plane APIs, reconciliation loops, or operator state can cause tenant-facing outages. Current manual canary processes require on-call intervention and are slow to detect degradations in multi-tenant private deployments.

Proposal summary: Build a reproducible canary orchestration script + Terraform-friendly pattern and an automated rollback scorer that quantifies canary health and triggers safe rollbacks or pause-and-investigate windows. The outcome should enable repeatable, auditable canaries for private controlplane upgrades with minimal human-in-the-loop when gates pass/fail.

Design components:
1) Terraform module pattern: controlplane_upgrade_canary module that provisions a canary shadow cluster and a small set of synthetic tenants. Module exposes inputs for version, tenant-fraction, traffic-sampler configuration, and lifecycle hooks (preflight/postflight). Module will use existing private deployment modules but create isolated control-plane namespace and PVs to run a canary controlplane instance.
2) Canary orchestration script: stateless script (python) run from CI or ops runner that performs: - deploy canary version via module - run smoke probes (k8s api ops, reconciliation latency, operator queue depth) - schedule synthetic request generator with shard keys to exercise tenant reconciliation - collect metrics and traces from console/endpoints - compute rollback score using weighted metric buckets (latency, error-rate, reconciliation-failures, kv-cache-miss-prominence, operator-crashloop-rate).
3) Rollback scorer: numeric score 0..100 derived from normalized SLO deltas and anomaly signals. Score mapping: 0-30 pass, 31-50 unstable (pause and extend sampling window), 51+ auto-rollback. Scorer will include hysteresis to avoid flapping: require N consecutive evaluation windows (configurable) before auto-rollback.
4) Safety features: - Tenant fencing: synthetic tenants are isolated and clearly labeled so any side-effects don't touch production tenants. - Traffic shadowing option (non-invasive) and an explicit traffic-cut flag for promotion. - Manual approval webhook that intercepts if scorer reaches unstable bucket. - Automatic snapshot + state-export before promotion to allow forensic analysis and roll-forward attempts.
5) Observability and alerts: Integrate with Console dashboards and SLOs used by the scorer. Add a canary-specific dashboard and a composite health metric that the scorer consumes. Post-deploy synthetic transactions stored as named traces for bisection.
6) Terraform/CI integration: Publish canary module in registry and provide a terragrunt example for teams. Jenkins/GitHub Actions runner will invoke the orchestration script; success/failure sets CI status and creates an audit log entry in the control-plane audit bucket.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for rollout):
- Canary module creates isolated canary controlplane that can be torn down with 'terraform destroy' without manual cleanup.
- Orchestration script runs end-to-end from CI and returns stable/pass/fail decisions without manual steps for a seeded canary.
- Rollback scorer thresholds validated in staging against historical telemetry (test harness included).
- Integrated dashboard shows canary-specific metrics and a timestamped decision log.
- Runbook created: steps to override/hard-rollback and how to interpret scorer signals.

Non-goals: This ticket does not cover automated multi-region failover logic or full tenant-migration automation. It focuses on controlplane version canaries and immediate rollback safety for private deployments.
